clue.text: Shell container after soldiers have been and gone?

definitions.text: Shell container after soldiers have been and gone?

parts.words: Shell container after soldiers have been and gone?
parts.note: soldiers here are the thin strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg; once they have done their work, the empty shell is left sitting in its holder

explanation.surface: A spent ammunition case left lying around after troops have marched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' are British nursery fingers of toast dunked in a boiled egg, not troops; 'Shell' is the eggshell, not artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The small cup holding a boiled egg is what remains on the breakfast table with the empty shell once the toast strips are eaten.

clue.text: A crippled boat heading north passing round a republic

indicators.note: the turned string goes round the second a, enclosing it
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the opening words are turned backwards

parts.note: crippled means lame
a tug is a small boat that tows ships

explanation.surface: A disabled vessel steers northward, sailing round a country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' reads the first three pieces upwards; 'passing round' has that string enclose the second a.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American country governed as a republic.

clue.text: Scottish peasant caught animal in river?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the otter is a mammal that lives and hunts in rivers

explanation.surface: A Highland farm labourer catches a creature in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottar or cotter was a Scottish tenant farmer holding a cottage in return for labour.

clue.text: Homework material located at foot of page

indicators.note: in a down clue the fabric sits below the page letter, coming after it

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery

explanation.surface: School homework printed in the footnote area of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: In British boarding schools, prep (short for preparation) is the set evening study period or homework.

clue.text: Arab quarter with money unlimited, blast!

indicators.note: unlimited here says the word for money loses its final boundary letter

parts.note: cash means money
blast and bah are both exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone in an Arab district with unlimited funds still curses.
explanation.definitionFit: The casbah or kasbah is the old walled citadel quarter of a North African Arab city.

clue.text: Type of lens — treatment for trachoma

indicators.note: giving the word a treatment works its letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A special lens used in curing an eye disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Trachoma is an eye infection, so a lens treatment sounds medically plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: An achromat is a lens built to bring two colours to one focus, cutting colour fringing.

clue.text: Clever type? Second-rate wet!

parts.note: B is a second-rate grade, below A
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A sneer at a supposed genius: actually mediocre and feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' in British slang means feeble, which suits the insult but here it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a brain is an informal way of naming a highly intelligent person.

clue.text: Sadly rooms haven't good light at night in summer?

definitions.text: good light at night in summer?

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the rooms lack decent lighting during summer evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: this full moon falls near the autumn equinox, at the tail of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The full moon nearest the autumn equinox gives bright moonlight that once let farmers gather crops after dusk.

clue.text: Working for female, journalist is somewhat deprived of basic need

parts.note: someone working for a boss is under them
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist employed by a woman finds herself rather short of essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is the most basic need, so lacking enough nourishment means being partly deprived of it.

clue.text: Daydreaming? Keep up!

parts.note: a keep is the fortified tower of a castle
something up is aloft, raised into the sky

explanation.surface: A daydreamer is told sharply to stay alert and keep up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep up!' reads as an order, but splits into a noun (Keep) and an adverb (up).
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a visionary scheme with no foundation, the kind of fancy idle reverie produces.

clue.text: Note short time needed to produce document

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note worth two semibreves
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Jotting a quick note to produce official paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A brevet is an official warrant or commission, especially one granting a military rank.

clue.text: Something lit up that nuclear physicist may study as clever person

definitions.text: Something lit up that nuclear physicist may study
definitions.meaning: a vivid flash of electrical discharge, the sort of glowing particle event a physicist examines
an informal, often ironic, name for a quick-witted individual

explanation.surface: A scientist studies a glowing discharge and is praised as brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a brilliant flash of light, and the colloquial label for a lively intelligent person.

clue.text: Hit out at wild cat behind lair

indicators.note: behind places the cat after the lair in the answer

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A big cat lashes out from behind its den.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, attacking someone verbally.

clue.text: Some centenarians lying around in the country

indicators.note: lying around means the selected letters are turned to run backwards
some says only part of the word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A few very old people lounge about in their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks NARI from inside centenarians; 'lying around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation of south-west Asia, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Pessimistic old rocker rolling over — somehow fate is sealed

indicators.note: sealed means the shuffled letters are shut inside the turned word
rolling over flips the word so it reads backwards

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some other order

explanation.surface: An ageing rock fan, toppling over, decides his fate is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British rock-and-roll fan; 'rolling over' turns him backwards and 'sealed' shuts the jumbled letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeatist expects to lose, a gloomy outlook giving up before trying.

clue.text: Philosopher has seen God, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy, as an adjective, suggests an elaborate rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A thinker claims to have glimpsed the deity, or so I imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes the Cynic was a Greek thinker famed for living in a tub.

clue.text: Home with no loose change in Fiji? People leading a simple life maybe

definitions.text: People leading a simple life maybe

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Fiji's dollar divides into cents, its small coins

explanation.surface: Stuck at home, broke on a Pacific island, living simply.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocents are guileless people, unworldly and uncomplicated in how they live.

clue.text: Married a totally heartless trout and suffered pain

indicators.note: totally heartless strips out every inner letter, leaving only the two ends of the fish's name

parts.note: ached means suffered pain

explanation.surface: Wedded to an utterly cruel old crone, and suffering for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trout' in British slang is an unpleasant old woman, fitting the unhappy marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached describes someone in a committed relationship, so already taken or wed.

clue.text: Who orated freely, offering some hard stuff

indicators.note: freely says the letters move without constraint into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone who gave a speech without restraint offered a few tough words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard stuff' sounds like strong drink or tough talk, but means timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The dense inner core of a tree trunk is its hardest, most durable timber.

clue.text: Wreck international organisation, allowing Germany in

indicators.note: in, with allowing, places the country's letter inside the organisation

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organisation
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A world body is ruined by letting Germany join.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo can mean to ruin someone, bringing about their downfall.

clue.text: Something painful a famous Nonconformist said

indicators.note: said means the name is spoken and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: John Bunyan, author of The Pilgrim's Progress, was a Nonconformist preacher jailed for his faith

explanation.surface: A famous dissenting preacher remarked on something that hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonconformists were English Protestants outside the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling on the joint of the big toe is notoriously sore.

clue.text: Best stuff in first half of homily making one hysterical

indicators.note: in places the best part inside the shortened sermon
first half of keeps the opening three of the six letters

parts.note: a homily is a sermon
the cream is the best part of anything

explanation.surface: A preacher's prime material in the opening of a sermon drives someone to hysterics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrieking uncontrollably is a person who screams, overcome with emotion.

clue.text: Lift given by worship that exudes power

indicators.note: exudes means the letter seeps out of the word, leaving it behind

parts.note: praise is worship of God
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Uplift from a worship service that radiates spiritual strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to elevate it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Scottish king invading England uncannily

indicators.note: the king invades these words, sitting across their boundary

explanation.surface: A Scots monarch strangely marches into England.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan I was the eleventh-century King of Scots killed by Macbeth.

clue.text: The old woman is set up in old-style country

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: ma is mother, the old woman in slang

explanation.surface: Mum has settled in some quaint old land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand was officially called Siam until 1939, so the name is a dated one.

clue.text: This American in difficulty has imported Italian number-crunchers

indicators.note: imported brings the abbreviation into the middle of the jumbled letters
in difficulty means the words are in a mess, their letters jumbled

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: An American in trouble has brought in Italian accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in difficulty' jumbles the letters of This American; 'has imported' places the Italian abbreviation inside the jumble near its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunchers is slang for people who work with figures, such as mathematicians.

clue.text: From what we hear, requires massages

indicators.note: this phrase says a word's sound gives the entry

parts.note: requires means needs

explanation.surface: Apparently someone requires a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working muscles with the hands, as a masseur does.

clue.text: Aussie university being broadcast in old TV series

indicators.note: in places the broadcasting word inside the TV title

parts.note: M*A*S*H was a long-running American comedy set in a Korean War field hospital
a programme being broadcast is on

explanation.surface: An Australian university features in a vintage television show being aired.
explanation.definitionFit: Monash University in Melbourne is one of Australia's largest universities.
